mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the month-over-month change in FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of months where FEDFUNDS declines month-over-month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.3% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, prompting central bank intervention and reducing corporate earnings growth expectations, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where UNRATE > 4.3, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a contraction in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue growth prospects deteriorate, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of months where both HOUST and RSAFS decline month-over-month, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is <0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime (defined by declining industrial production and high inflation), a decline in INDPRO signals further supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate margins are squeezed.
regime_hint: supply shock regime: INDPRO decline and CPI annual inflation > 3.5%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where the supply shock regime is active (INDPRO decline and CPI annual inflation > 3.5%), or the Rank IC for the INDPRO signal in that regime is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of months where RSAFS increases month-over-month, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the annual inflation rate (measured by CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of months where CPIAUCSL annual change > 3.5%, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a monetary tightening cycle that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL > 3.5%, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A strong GDP growth rate (measured by the quarterly change in GDPC1) in the most recent quarter signals a late-cycle expansion, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy approaches a peak.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of quarters where GDPC1 growth rate is above 2.0%, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is <0.03.
